title: Burp Setup — Proxy, CA Cert, Scope, Extensions, Project Config
body: Everything here is a one-time cost that pays back every engagement. CA cert not installed = HTTPS is useless. Scope not set = 2000 noise requests drown the 20 that matter. Intercept left ON = browser hangs. Project files (Pro) mean you never lose a request. The extension stack (Param Miner, Autorize, JWT Editor, Turbo Intruder) doubles what Burp Community can find. Configure this once per engagement, not per session.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ SETUP CHECKLIST — do in this order ══════════════════════════════

# 1) BROWSER PROXY — FoxyProxy (one-click toggle, never dig into settings again)
# Install FoxyProxy Standard (Firefox extension)
# Add proxy: Title=Burp, Host=127.0.0.1, Port=8080
# Toggle on/off per engagement. Save Firefox profile with Burp settings.

# 2) CA CERT — HTTPS decryption (CRITICAL, do before anything else)
# Browse to http://burpsuite -> "CA Certificate" -> save burp-cacert.der
# Firefox: Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Certificates -> View Certificates
#          -> Authorities -> Import -> select burp-cacert.der -> trust for websites
# Chrome/Chromium:  Settings -> Privacy -> Manage certificates -> Authorities -> Import
# System-wide (Kali): sudo cp burp-cacert.der /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/burp.crt
#                     sudo update-ca-certificates
# Verify: browse https://target.com -> Burp cert shows as issuer, no TLS error

# 3) SCOPE — define it immediately, before browsing
# Target tab -> right-click the host -> Add to scope
# OR Target -> Scope -> Include in scope -> add host/domain regex
# Proxy -> Options -> tick "And URL is in target scope"
#   -> now only scoped requests log to HTTP History (kills CDN/analytics noise)
# Response scope: Options -> "Don't send items to Proxy history or live tasks"
#   when URL not in scope -> saves RAM on long engagements

# 4) PROJECT FILE (Pro) — save state between sessions
# Burp -> New project from disk -> name it <target>-<date>.burp
# Saves: all HTTP history, Repeater tabs, Intruder configs, Scanner results, notes
# End of session: File -> Save copy -> pick the .burp file
# Resume: Burp -> Open existing project -> your .burp file

# 5) INTERCEPT — OFF by default
# Proxy -> Intercept -> click "Intercept is on" to toggle off
# Use HTTP History as your primary view — it shows everything without blocking
# Turn Intercept ON only when you need to modify a specific request mid-flight

# 6) INTERCEPT SERVER RESPONSES (enable selectively)
# Proxy -> Options -> Intercept Server Responses -> "Intercept responses..."
# Add rule: when request was intercepted (already modifying the request)
# Or: add a rule for specific paths (e.g., path matches /admin/*)
# Needed for: removing JS-side validation, editing a 302 to 200, injecting content

# ══ PROJECT OPTIONS — configure once ════════════════════════════════
# Project options -> Connections -> Upstream proxy (for chaining through corp proxy)
# Project options -> Sessions -> Session Handling Rules (auto refresh CSRF token)
# Project options -> Misc -> Logging (log all requests to file for offline grep)

# ══ ESSENTIAL EXTENSIONS — install from BApp Store ══════════════════
# Burp -> Extensions -> BApp Store -> search and install:
#
# Param Miner (PortSwigger) — FREE
#   Find hidden GET/POST params, headers, cookies by diffing response changes.
#   Right-click request -> Extensions -> Param Miner -> Guess everything
#   Output: Extensions tab -> Param Miner -> Output
#
# Autorize (Barak Tawily) — FREE
#   Replay every request as a lower-privilege user to detect IDOR / authz bypass.
#   Set "Interception filters" to your low-priv session cookie.
#   Browse as high-priv user -> Autorize replays each request as low-priv.
#   Green=enforced, Red=bypassed, Yellow=modified but not enforced.
#
# JWT Editor (PortSwigger) — FREE
#   Decode, edit, and re-sign JWTs directly in Burp.
#   New Key -> generate RSA/HMAC key. In Repeater -> JSON Web Token tab.
#   Attack: "Embedded JWK", "HMAC key confusion", "None algorithm" all built-in.
#
# Logger++ (Netsparker/free) — FREE
#   Full request/response log with grep filter on any field.
#   Filter syntax: Request.Path contains "/api/" && Response.Status == 200
#   Export: save all matching requests to CSV/file for offline analysis.
#
# Turbo Intruder (PortSwigger) — FREE
#   High-speed Intruder replacement. Critical for race conditions.
#   Uses Python scripts for attack logic. Single-packet attack built-in.
#   Send to Turbo Intruder -> select template -> edit -> run
#
# Active Scan++ (albinowax) — FREE (Pro scanner required for some checks)
#   Extends scanner with SSRF, SSTI, RCE probes, header injection.
#
# Retire.js (PortSwigger) — FREE
#   Flags vulnerable JS libraries (jQuery, Angular, Bootstrap etc) in responses.
#   Results appear in Target -> Site map -> Issues automatically.

# ══ ROUTING TOOLS THROUGH BURP ══════════════════════════════════════
# Python requests:
import requests
proxies={'http':'http://127.0.0.1:8080','https':'http://127.0.0.1:8080'}
requests.get('https://target.com', proxies=proxies, verify=False)
# curl:   curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 -k https://target.com
# sqlmap: sqlmap -u '...' --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080
# ffuf:   ffuf -u '...' -replay-proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080
# nmap:   via proxychains (proxychains4 nmap ...) — TCP only
# git:    git config http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080
warn: CA cert is the #1 setup failure — without it HTTPS responses show only encrypted bytes and nothing useful. Always verify it worked by browsing any HTTPS site through Burp and checking the certificate issuer. Set scope before you do anything else or your HTTP History will be overwhelmed. Project files are why Burp Pro is worth it on long engagements — never lose a request.
